title: Care home rota with meds-trained seniors and a twilight shift
notes: Long days (8-8) and nights (8-8) each have a senior row that needs 'meds' in the competencies list and a carer row; the twilight (5pm-10pm) overlaps the end of the day and the start of the night, so 'nobody on two shifts at once' binds, and a twilight followed by the next day's 8am start is a 10-hour gap, so the 11-hour rule binds too. Gary and Rhona, and Kemi and Bernadette, are carers without meds, so 'the same shift' can only mean the same carer row. The reference score 0 is optimal (proven by the reviewer's exact search): the four bank staff work 29 hours each and no soft rule is violated. Disruption: Wendy is ill on Wednesday 9 December (she works the day carer slot); a feasible re-plan exists (hard 0). Sources (facts only, changed where useful): care home day shifts 8am-8pm and nights 8pm-8am, typically 3 to 4 shifts a week (job adverts seen through the search index; the pages need JavaScript) - https://www.carehome.co.uk/jobs/job.cfm/id/96009114415 ; staff who give medicines are trained and assessed as competent - https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/sc1 ; 11 hours of rest between working days - https://www.gov.uk/rest-breaks-work
